group.title: Everyday A1
sources: Word choice guided by general-purpose and academic frequency ideas (NGSL and AWL families); all meanings and sentences are original.

words.meaning: Feeling pleased and cheerful.
examples: Mina was {happy} when her friend called.
wrong: I am happy because my dog is very sick.
Yesterday she happy to see us.

words.meaning: To get something by paying money for it.
examples: We {buy} bread at the corner shop.
wrong: I buy a new coat, so the shop pays me money.
Yesterday I buy a new phone.

words.meaning: The room where people cook food.
examples: Dad is making soup in the {kitchen}.
wrong: We take a hot shower in the kitchen.
A kitchen is a person who cooks.

words.meaning: An opening in a wall that lets in light and air.
examples: Please open the {window}; it is hot.
wrong: It is freezing, so please open the window wide.
She cut the bread with a window.

words.meaning: In a short time; fast.
examples: She ate her breakfast {quickly} and ran to school.
wrong: He walked quickly, so he arrived after a very long hour.
She is a very quickly runner.

words.meaning: Needing rest or sleep.
examples: I am {tired} after a long day at work.
wrong: I slept ten hours, so I am very tired and full of energy.
She tired very much last night.

words.meaning: A person you like and know well.
examples: My {friend} lives next door.
wrong: A friend is someone you do not know at all.
He friend me a book yesterday.

words.meaning: To prepare food by heating it.
examples: I {cook} rice for dinner every evening.
wrong: I cooked dinner with cold water and no heat.
She cooks the television for dinner.

words.meaning: The sun, rain, wind or cold outside.
examples: The {weather} is sunny today.
wrong: The weather is my brother's name.
The weathers are sunny today.

words.meaning: A road in a town with buildings on the sides.
examples: The bakery is on the next {street}.
wrong: We drive on the street from the kitchen to the bedroom.
I sat on the streets and read a street.

words.meaning: Before the usual or expected time.
examples: We arrived {early} and waited for the doors to open.
wrong: I arrived early, so I missed the beginning of the film.
She comes early than me.

words.meaning: A place where people buy and sell food and goods.
examples: Grandma buys fresh fish at the {market}.
wrong: The market is a room where we sleep.
He markets yesterday to buy apples.

words.meaning: To clean something with water.
examples: Please {wash} your hands before lunch.
wrong: I wash my hands with dirty sand.
He washes his car yesterday.

words.meaning: A place where you can read or borrow books.
examples: She borrowed three books from the {library}.
wrong: We buy bread at the library.
A library is a kind of soup.

words.meaning: A piece of paper that lets you enter or travel.
examples: I need a {ticket} for the train.
wrong: A ticket is a kind of soup.
The ticket was cheap, so it cost one thousand dollars.

words.meaning: To take something and give it back later.
examples: Can I {borrow} your pen for a minute?
wrong: I borrow my sister a pen.
Please borrow me your pen and keep it forever.

words.meaning: The day each year when you were born.
examples: Her {birthday} is in March.
wrong: My birthday is every day of the week.
Today is my birthday of the winter.

words.meaning: The meal you eat in the middle of the day.
examples: We have {lunch} at noon.
wrong: I eat lunch at midnight, before breakfast.
She lunches a letter.

words.meaning: Paying attention so you do not make a mistake or get hurt.
examples: Be {careful}; the floor is wet.
wrong: He was very careful, so he fell down three times.
She is careful at the stairs of.

words.meaning: To not be able to find something.
examples: Don't {lose} your keys again.
wrong: I lose my keys, so I know exactly where they are.
He lose his wallet yesterday.

words.meaning: A room where you sleep.
examples: My {bedroom} has a small desk and a lamp.
wrong: We cook dinner in the bedroom oven.
He bedroomed a cold shower.

words.meaning: To say or write something after a question.
examples: Please {answer} the phone.
wrong: I answer a question before anyone asks me.
She answers to the question of the teacher.

words.meaning: Not costing much money.
examples: These shoes were {cheap}, so I bought two pairs.
wrong: The shoes were cheap, so they cost a lot of money.
This is the most cheap shop.

words.meaning: To go and see a person or place for a short time.
examples: We {visit} my grandparents on Sundays.
wrong: I visit my aunt and I never see her.
She visits to her aunt on Sundays.

words.meaning: A person who lives near you.
examples: Our {neighbor} waters our plants when we travel.
wrong: My neighbor lives in another country, far from my house.
She neighbors very kind.

words.meaning: A container with a narrow neck for liquid.
examples: He drank water from a plastic {bottle}.
wrong: I put the milk in a bottle made of paper with no lid and no bottom.
She bottles of water on the table.

words.meaning: To pay attention to a sound.
examples: I like to {listen} to music on the bus.
wrong: I listen the radio with my eyes.
He listens a book on the shelf.

words.meaning: Prepared and able to start.
examples: Dinner is {ready}; come and eat.
wrong: I am ready, so I need one more hour to start.
She readies for school.

words.meaning: With nothing inside.
examples: The box was {empty}, so I threw it away.
wrong: The glass is empty and full of juice.
He emptys the bottle yesterday.

words.meaning: To like doing or having something.
examples: I {enjoy} walking in the park.
wrong: I enjoy going to the dentist because I hate it.
She enjoys to swim.

words.meaning: A structure that lets people cross a river.
examples: We walked across the {bridge} to the other side.
wrong: We swam under the bridge to the top of the sky.
A bridge is a kind of fruit.

words.meaning: To rest with your eyes closed at night.
examples: Babies {sleep} a lot.
wrong: I sleep with my eyes open and talk all night.
He sleeped well last night.

words.meaning: A short coat.
examples: Take a {jacket}; it may get cold.
wrong: She ate a jacket for breakfast.
He jacket his coat on the chair.

words.meaning: Wanting to eat.
examples: I am {hungry}; let's have lunch.
wrong: I am hungry because I just ate three big meals.
She is hungry of a sandwich.

words.meaning: To hold something and take it from one place to another.
examples: Can you {carry} this bag for me?
wrong: I carry the weather in my hand.
He carried the bag to he home.

words.meaning: A very small town in the countryside.
examples: My grandparents live in a quiet {village}.
wrong: The village has two million people and a huge airport.
She villages to work by bus.

words.meaning: To say or do something again.
examples: Please {repeat} the question.
wrong: I repeat the word once and only one time.
He repeat the song again.

words.meaning: Very nice to look at or hear.
examples: The garden looks {beautiful} in spring.
wrong: The garden looks very beautiful and ugly.
She sings beautiful.

words.meaning: An idea about what you will do.
examples: What is your {plan} for the weekend?
wrong: I put my plan in the oven for ten minutes.
He plans of the dog a shoe.

words.meaning: Not dirty.
examples: Please put on a {clean} shirt.
wrong: The floor is clean because it is covered with mud.
He is clean the room now.
